name: dwc3_get_dr_mode
prose: dwc3_get_dr_mode(dwc) (core.c:53-109). Precondition: dwc is an initialised struct dwc3 with dev and hwparams.hwparams0 valid. Postcondition: if dwc->dr_mode is USB_DR_MODE_UNKNOWN it is first set to USB_DR_MODE_OTG, silently. The hardware mode is read from hwparams0. For gadget-only hardware it returns -EINVAL (with an error message) if CONFIG_USB_DWC3_HOST is enabled, else the target mode is USB_DR_MODE_PERIPHERAL; for host-only hardware it returns -EINVAL if CONFIG_USB_DWC3_GADGET is enabled, else the target mode is USB_DR_MODE_HOST. For other (dual-role) hardware the target mode starts as the current dr_mode, becomes HOST if CONFIG_USB_DWC3_HOST is enabled or else PERIPHERAL if CONFIG_USB_DWC3_GADGET is enabled, and an OTG result is turned into PERIPHERAL when there is no extcon device, the kernel has no CONFIG_USB_ROLE_SWITCH or the device has no "usb-role-switch" property, and the IP is not a DWC3 older than 3.30a. If the target differs from dwc->dr_mode (as it is after the UNKNOWN-to-OTG default), a "Configuration mismatch" warning naming host or gadget is printed and dwc->dr_mode is set to the target; the UNKNOWN-to-OTG default by itself prints nothing. It returns 0 in those cases. On the two -EINVAL returns dwc->dr_mode has at most been changed from UNKNOWN to OTG.
note: reviewer RIGHT (R15): the UNKNOWN->OTG assignment at lines 59-60 is silent; the warning at 100-105 is only for a later difference; R2 (-EINVAL after UNKNOWN->OTG) was already stated

name: __dwc3_gadget_ep_queue
prose: __dwc3_gadget_ep_queue(dep, req) (gadget.c:1989-2053). Precondition: dep and req are valid and req is not currently queued. Postcondition: returns -ESHUTDOWN, without touching req, if dep->endpoint.desc is NULL or dwc->pullups_connected or dwc->connected is false. It returns -EINVAL, with a WARN and without modifying req, if req->dep != dep or req->status < DWC3_REQUEST_STATUS_COMPLETED. Otherwise it calls pm_runtime_get(dwc->dev) (not released here), sets req->request.actual = 0 and request.status = -EINPROGRESS, appends req to dep->pending_list and sets req->status = DWC3_REQUEST_STATUS_QUEUED. Then it returns 0 without starting anything if DWC3_EP_WAIT_TRANSFER_COMPLETE is set; returns 0 after setting DWC3_EP_DELAY_START if any of DWC3_EP_END_TRANSFER_PENDING, DWC3_EP_WEDGE, DWC3_EP_DELAY_STOP or DWC3_EP_STALL is set; for an isochronous endpoint whose transfer has not started returns the result of __dwc3_gadget_start_isoc(dep) if DWC3_EP_PENDING_REQUEST is set (it can be nonzero) and 0 otherwise; in all remaining cases (including an isochronous endpoint whose transfer has started) it calls __dwc3_gadget_kick_transfer(dep), ignores its result and returns 0.
note: reviewer WRONG (R15): the final path is '__dwc3_gadget_kick_transfer(dep); return 0;' (lines 2050-2052), the result is ignored as the prose said; R1 start_isoc point was already in the prose

name: dwc3_gadget_init
prose: Slice cut the head: dwc3_gadget_init(dwc) (gadget.c:4833-4958). Precondition: dwc is a struct dwc3 with sysdev, dev, num_eps, maximum_speed and max_ssp_rate set and gadget not yet created. Postcondition: it gets the gadget IRQ with dwc3_gadget_get_irq (peripheral, then dwc_usb3, then the first platform IRQ); a negative value is returned at once. dwc->irq_gadget is then set (and stays set on later failures). It allocates, in order, dwc->ep0_trb (coherent, -ENOMEM), dwc->setup_buf (kzalloc) and dwc->bounce (coherent), initialises ep0_in_setup, err_recovery_work and connect_mutex, allocates dwc->gadget (kzalloc; failure is -ENOMEM and goes to the label that frees only the three earlier buffers, usb_put_gadget is not called), initialises it with usb_initialize_gadget and fills in its fields, calls dwc3_gadget_init_endpoints (failure: usb_put_gadget(dwc->gadget), dwc->gadget set to NULL, then bounce, setup_buf and ep0_trb freed, error returned) and usb_add_gadget (failure: the endpoints are freed first and then the same unwinding, error returned). On success it sets the speed or SSP rate with dwc3_gadget_set_ssp_rate / dwc3_gadget_set_speed, calls device_wakeup_disable(dwc->sysdev) if dwc->sys_wakeup is set and returns 0; the buffers and gadget stay owned by dwc until dwc3_gadget_exit.
note: reviewer RIGHT (R15): the gadget kzalloc failure frees only ep0_trb/setup_buf/bounce and never calls usb_put_gadget (4872-4876, 4945-4954); old prose said usb_put_gadget on every failure

name: _dbgp_external_startup
prose: Slice cut the head: _dbgp_external_startup (ehci-dbgp.c:490-606), a static function with no parameters that uses the globals ehci_regs, ehci_debug and dbgp_phys_port. Postcondition: it calls dbgp_ehci_startup(); a nonzero result (-ENODEV when the controller does not leave the halted state) is returned at once. It then waits for a device on the debug port with ehci_wait_for_port. If that fails and the port shows no connection, once only it clears CMD_RUN, sets PORT_TEST_PKT, delays 50 ms, calls dbgp_ehci_controller_reset() (result ignored) and starts over from dbgp_ehci_startup; otherwise it starts over once more (reset_port_tries); after that it returns -EIO ("No device found in debug port"). It then sets DBGP_CLAIM in the debug control register; if the bit does not stick it clears it and returns -ENODEV. Otherwise it clears PORT_PE and waits 100 ms. It then (up to four passes in total) scans device numbers 0 to 127 for a GET_DESCRIPTOR of the debug descriptor that returns data, records the debug endpoints, moves the device to address 127 with SET_ADDRESS if it was elsewhere, sends SET_FEATURE(DEBUG_MODE) and does a one-byte bulk write; any failed step or not finding the device retries from the scan and, when the retries are used up, returns -ENODEV. On success it sets dbgp_not_safe = 0 and returns 0.
note: reviewer R1 RIGHT (reset result is ignored); old prose rechecked; slice cut head; contract dropped because the function reads and writes globals and hardware

name: qh_urb_transaction
prose: Slice cut the head: the function is qh_urb_transaction(fotg210, urb, head, flags) (fotg210-hcd.c:2522-2684), which builds the qtd list for an URB. Precondition: urb has its transfer buffer or scatterlist DMA-mapped; head is a list head owned by the caller; flags are GFP flags. Postcondition: it allocates one qtd, links it on head and, for a control pipe, fills it as the SETUP stage and allocates a second qtd for the data or status stage. It then splits the transfer buffer (or each scatterlist entry, limited by the transfer length) into as many qtds as qtd_fill needs, allocating each new one and linking it on head. After the last data qtd it sets hw_alt_next to the list end unless URB_SHORT_NOT_OK is set on a non-control URB. Only when transfer_buffer_length is nonzero it adds one more zero-length qtd: for control transfers a status-stage qtd in the opposite direction with DATA1, and for an OUT transfer with URB_ZERO_PACKET only if the length is an exact multiple of maxpacket. It sets QTD_IOC in the last qtd unless URB_NO_INTERRUPT is set and returns head. If any qtd allocation fails it calls qtd_list_free(fotg210, urb, head), which frees the qtds on head, and returns NULL.
note: reviewer RIGHT (R15): the terminating qtd is only added when transfer_buffer_length != 0 (2650), and zero-packet needs length % maxpacket == 0 (2657-2659); control URBs always have a setup qtd and a data/status qtd

name: fotg210_udc_probe
prose: Slice cut the head: the function is fotg210_udc_probe(pdev, fotg) (fotg210-udc.c:1173-1306); the item showed only its error tail. Precondition: pdev is the platform device; fotg is the shared fotg210 structure whose base is mapped by the caller. Postcondition: returns the platform_get_irq error if the IRQ is negative; -ENOMEM if the fotg210_udc allocation fails. It looks up the optional PHY (-EPROBE_DEFER is an error that frees the allocation and is returned, other lookup errors mean no PHY; a usb_phy_init failure is returned the same way). It allocates the FOTG210_MAX_NUM_EP endpoint structures (-ENOMEM on failure), sets up the gadget and endpoints, allocates the ep0 request (-ENOMEM on failure), initialises the hardware, requests the shared IRQ (error returned), registers the PHY notifier if a PHY exists and calls usb_add_gadget_udc. On success it returns 0. The error labels undo in this order: on usb_add_gadget_udc failure the notifier (if a PHY exists) and the IRQ; then the ep0 request; then iounmap(fotg210->reg) (the register mapping owned by the caller's fotg); then every endpoint allocation; then the udc allocation; the error from the failing step is returned. An endpoint allocation failure skips the ep0-request and iounmap steps; the PHY is not shut down on any error path.
note: slice cut head; real function fotg210_udc_probe; old prose treated the tail as the whole function and said an 'ioremap' is undone, but the mapping belongs to fotg (iounmap of fotg210->reg at 1297 runs on the ep0-request, request_irq and add_udc failures only)

name: composite_setup
prose: Slice cut the head: composite_setup(gadget, ctrl) (composite.c:1754-2286). Precondition: gadget is a registered composite gadget (get_gadget_data gives cdev with an ep0 request cdev->req and a buffer of USB_COMP_EP0_BUFSIZ bytes); ctrl is the setup packet. Postcondition: value starts as -EOPNOTSUPP. If wLength exceeds USB_COMP_EP0_BUFSIZ, an OUT request returns -EOPNOTSUPP at once; an IN request has ctrl->wLength overwritten (through a const cast) with USB_COMP_EP0_BUFSIZ and continues. It re-initialises cdev->req (zero 0, context cdev, complete composite_setup_complete, length 0) and sets ep0->driver_data. Non-standard request types go to the "unknown" path; standard ones are handled by bRequest: GET_DESCRIPTOR (IN only: device, qualifier and other-speed config for dual-speed non-SuperSpeed gadgets, config, string, BOS, OTG), SET_CONFIGURATION (bRequestType 0; takes cdev->lock and calls set_config), GET_CONFIGURATION, SET_INTERFACE and GET_INTERFACE (via the function's set_alt/get_alt; a DELAYED_STATUS result increments cdev->delayed_status), GET_STATUS (OTG HNP polling, or the SuperSpeed interface status through f->get_status) and CLEAR/SET_FEATURE (SuperSpeed FUNCTION_SUSPEND through f->func_suspend or the default wakeup/suspend handling); anything else is "unknown". The unknown path handles OS-descriptor vendor requests, WebUSB URL requests, then looks for a function (req_match, interface or endpoint recipient) or the configuration's own setup callback and returns that callback's value directly through the done label, without queuing a reply here. The cases that end at check_value, when value >= 0 and is not USB_GADGET_DELAYED_STATUS, set req->length = value and zero = value < w_length and queue the reply with composite_ep0_queue(GFP_ATOMIC); if that fails the status is cleared and composite_setup_complete is called; ep0 is not halted here. The function returns value: 0 after a successful queue, a negative errno (including -EOPNOTSUPP for unhandled requests and the queue error), USB_GADGET_DELAYED_STATUS, or the raw value of a function or configuration setup callback. No lock is held on return.
note: reviewer RIGHT (R15): composite_setup does not halt ep0 when the queue fails (2271-2276); old prose said it did and described only a subset of paths

name: set_config
prose: Slice cut the head: set_config(cdev, ctrl, number) (composite.c:947-1063). Precondition: cdev and ctrl are valid; number is the configuration value (0 means unconfigure); the caller (composite_setup) holds cdev->lock. Postcondition: power starts at 8 mA (OTG gadget) or 100 mA. If number is nonzero, the configuration with that bConfigurationValue is looked up; if none exists result is -EINVAL and nothing changes (cdev->config, the gadget state and all functions untouched); if found, any current configuration is first reset (reset_config: each function's disable callback, func_wakeup_armed cleared, endpoint bitmap zeroed, cdev->config = NULL and delayed_status = 0). If number is 0 any current configuration is reset and result is 0. For a found configuration c the gadget state becomes USB_STATE_CONFIGURED, cdev->config = c and, for each interface function up to the first NULL slot, the endpoints in the descriptors for the current speed are recorded in f->endpoints and f->set_alt(f, slot, 0) is called; a negative result calls reset_config(cdev) and stops with that result (the gadget state stays CONFIGURED); a USB_GADGET_DELAYED_STATUS result increments cdev->delayed_status. If all succeed the power becomes c->MaxPower (or CONFIG_USB_GADGET_VBUS_DRAW when MaxPower is 0 and c is not self-powered), limited to 500 mA below SuperSpeed and 900 mA otherwise, and remote wakeup is set according to USB_CONFIG_ATT_WAKEUP. All paths then reach the same tail (including number 0 and the -EINVAL and set_alt-failure cases): self-powered is cleared if power > USB_SELF_POWER_VBUS_MAX_DRAW or c is non-NULL and not self-powered, otherwise set; usb_gadget_vbus_draw(gadget, power) is called with the power above (the default 8 or 100 on the number 0, -EINVAL and set_alt failure paths); and if result is non-negative and cdev->delayed_status is nonzero the result becomes USB_GADGET_DELAYED_STATUS. It returns result.
note: reviewer WRONG (R15): number 0 and invalid numbers do reach the done tail which sets self-powered and the vbus draw (1052-1059); old prose wrongly said the default power is clamped to 500/900 mA (clamping only happens after a successful configuration, 1043-1046)

name: handle_exception
prose: Slice cut the head: handle_exception(common) (f_mass_storage.c:2434-2564). Precondition: common is an initialised struct fsg_common; common->state and exception_arg describe a pending exception. Postcondition: returns nothing. It first dequeues every pending signal; any signal other than SIGUSR1 sets common->state = FSG_STATE_EXIT under common->lock. If common->fsg is set, then for each of the fsg_num_buffers buffers it dequeues the bulk-in request if the buffer is BUF_STATE_SENDING and the bulk-out request if BUF_STATE_RECEIVING and calls sleep_thread(common, false, bh); if that returns nonzero (-EINTR) the function returns at once, leaving the buffer states, buffer pointers and common->state as they are at that moment (state may already be FSG_STATE_EXIT), without running the exception handling and with no lock held. Otherwise it flushes the enabled bulk FIFOs and, under common->lock, sets all buffers to BUF_STATE_EMPTY, sets both buffer pointers to buffhds[0], saves exception_req_tag, new_fsg = exception_arg and old_state, sets state to FSG_STATE_NORMAL and, unless old_state was FSG_STATE_ABORT_BULK_OUT, clears prevent_medium_removal, sense data, unit attention data, sense info and info_valid in every non-NULL LUN. After unlocking it acts on old_state: FSG_STATE_NORMAL, nothing; ABORT_BULK_OUT, send_status; PROTOCOL_RESET, if fsg is set, test-and-clear IGNORE_BULK_OUT and clear the bulk-in halt if it was set, and ep0_queue when ep0_req_tag equals the saved tag; CONFIG_CHANGE, do_set_interface(common, new_fsg) and usb_composite_setup_continue if new_fsg is non-NULL; EXIT, do_set_interface(common, NULL) and then state = FSG_STATE_TERMINATED under the lock; TERMINATED, nothing.
note: reviewer WRONG (R15): FSG_STATE_TERMINATED is its own case that only breaks (2561-2562), it is not grouped with EXIT; R1/R2 early-return points were already in the prose

name: do_write
prose: Slice cut the head: do_write(common) (f_mass_storage.c:738-922). Precondition: common->curlun is valid and common->cmnd holds a WRITE(6), WRITE(10), WRITE(12) or WRITE(16) CDB. Postcondition: the value it returns is negative. If the LUN is read-only it sets SS_WRITE_PROTECTED and returns -EINVAL. Otherwise it clears O_SYNC on the backing file, then for WRITE(6) takes the 24-bit LBA, and for the others takes the 32- or 64-bit LBA, returns -EINVAL with SS_INVALID_FIELD_IN_CDB if any CDB byte-1 bit other than DPO/FUA (0x18) is set, and sets O_SYNC on the file when FUA is set and nofua is clear. An LBA at or beyond num_sectors sets SS_LOGICAL_BLOCK_ADDRESS_OUT_OF_RANGE and returns -EINVAL. It then loops: it queues bulk-out requests of up to FSG_BUFLEN bytes (-EIO if start_out_transfer fails; beyond the file end it sets the out-of-range sense and stops requesting), waits with sleep_thread for each buffer (returning its -EINTR), handles a failed bulk-out status (SS_COMMUNICATION_FAILURE, stop), trims the received amount to the file length, the intended length and whole blocks, writes it with kernel_write (returning -EINTR if a signal is pending after the write; a negative or short write sets SS_WRITE_ERROR and stops), updates file_offset, amount_left_to_write and common->residue, and stops with short_packet_received set if the host sent less than intended. When the loop is left by any break or by completion the function returns -EIO ("no default reply"); sense_data, sense_data_info and info_valid are set on the error cases above.
note: reviewer WRONG (R15): O_SYNC is cleared at the start (755) so it is not left set; slice cut the head

name: ncm_setup
prose: Slice cut the head: ncm_setup(f, ctrl) (f_ncm.c:679-856). Precondition: f is a bound NCM function (f->config->cdev valid); ctrl is the control request; cdev->req has a buffer big enough for sizeof(ntb_parameters). Postcondition: it handles these class requests addressed to the control interface (wIndex must equal ncm->ctrl_id): SET_ETHERNET_PACKET_FILTER (OUT, wLength 0; stores wValue in port.cdc_filter; reply length 0), GET_NTB_PARAMETERS (IN, wLength nonzero, wValue 0; copies min(wLength, sizeof ntb_parameters) bytes; that is the reply length), GET_NTB_INPUT_SIZE (IN, wLength at least 4; 4 bytes of fixed_in_len), SET_NTB_INPUT_SIZE (OUT, wLength 4; sets req->complete to ncm_ep0out_complete, length 4 and context f), GET_NTB_FORMAT (IN, wLength at least 2; 2 bytes), SET_NTB_FORMAT (OUT, wLength 0, wValue 0 or 1 selects ndp16 or ndp32 parser_opts), GET_CRC_MODE (IN, wLength at least 2; 2 bytes) and SET_CRC_MODE (OUT, wLength 0, wValue 0 or 1 sets is_crc). Any other request or a malformed one leaves value -EOPNOTSUPP. In every case ncm->ndp_sign is recomputed from parser_opts->ndp_sign and is_crc. When value is non-negative it sets req->zero = 0, req->length = value and returns the result of usb_ep_queue(ep0, req, GFP_ATOMIC) (logging a failure); otherwise it returns -EOPNOTSUPP without queueing.
note: reviewer RIGHT (R15): the reply length is min(wLength, sizeof ntb_parameters) for GET_NTB_PARAMETERS (726-728), not just 0/2/4/w_length; the old prose also stated lengths loosely

name: UAC1_RATE_ATTRIBUTE(name)
prose: Macro-generated function f_uac1_opts_<name>_show(item, page) (for c_srate and p_srate, reading opts->c_srates / p_srates) from UAC1_RATE_ATTRIBUTE(name) (f_uac1.c:1570). Precondition: item is a config_item embedded in a f_uac1_opts; page is a PAGE_SIZE buffer. Postcondition: it takes opts->lock with mutex_lock, sets page[0] = 0, then appends "%u," for each element of the rate array up to UAC_MAX_RATES, stopping at the first element equal to 0; if page is then non-empty the final ',' is replaced by '\n'. It releases the lock and returns the number of bytes appended by sprintf (0 and an empty page when the first element is 0).
note: macro-generated; R15 comment concerned the store function; show prose rechecked

name: UAC1_RATE_ATTRIBUTE(name)
prose: Macro-generated function f_uac1_opts_<name>_store(item, page, len) from UAC1_RATE_ATTRIBUTE(name) (f_uac1.c:1570). Precondition: item is embedded in a f_uac1_opts; page is a NUL-terminated string. Postcondition: it takes opts->lock and returns -EBUSY (nothing changed) if opts->refcnt is nonzero. Otherwise it zeroes the rate array, duplicates page with kstrdup (the result is not checked: on failure the loop does not run and the function returns -EINVAL with the array left zeroed), splits the copy on commas and for each token calls kstrtou32(token, 0, &num): a parse error is returned as is (kstrtou32 can give -EINVAL or -ERANGE) with the entries stored so far kept; more than UAC_MAX_RATES tokens give -EINVAL with the array full; each stored token sets the result to len. On success it returns len. The copy is freed and the lock released on each return after the lock was taken.
note: reviewer RIGHT (R15): the kstrdup result is not checked (1612) so failure yields -EINVAL with zeroed array, and too many tokens leaves a full array (1618-1622); old prose said partially filled

name: uvc_function_bind
prose: Slice cut the head: uvc_function_bind(c, f) (f_uvc.c:664-901). Precondition: f belongs to a UVC function instance whose f->fi is an f_uvc_opts; opts->lock is not held on entry. Postcondition: it sets uvc->func_unbound = false under uvc->lock, clamps the streaming parameters in opts, fills in the FS/HS/SS streaming endpoint descriptors and autoconfigures the optional interrupt endpoint and the streaming endpoint; failure of either returns -EINVAL (the initial value of ret) through the error label. It then takes opts->lock, fixes up extension-unit string ids, attaches the strings (error returned), allocates two interface ids (error returned) and copies the FS, HS, SS and SSP descriptors (error returned); those failures release opts->lock and go through the label that also calls v4l2_device_unregister (although it was not registered at that point) and then frees the control request and buffer and all descriptors. On success of the copies it releases opts->lock, allocates the ep0 control request and buffer (failure: -ENOMEM through the error label, which does not call v4l2_device_unregister), registers the V4L2 device (on failure it jumps to the error label with ret still holding the last interface id, so the function returns that non-negative value), calls uvcg_video_init and uvc_register_video (a negative result goes through the label that unregisters the V4L2 device) and returns 0. On success the endpoints, descriptors, request/buffer and V4L2 and video devices stay owned by the function until unbind.
note: reviewer RIGHT (R15): the control-req/buf and v4l2_device_register failures go to 'error' and skip v4l2_device_unregister (859-871, 887-891); opts->lock is held only on the error_unlock paths

name: UVCG_DEFAULT_PROCESSING_ATTR(cname, aname, bits)

name: UVCG_EXTENSION_ATTR(i_extension, iExtension, _RO)
prose: Macro-generated function uvcg_extension_i_extension_show(item, page) from UVCG_EXTENSION_ATTR(i_extension, iExtension, _RO) (uvc_configfs.c:787-811). Precondition: item is the config_item of the i_extension attribute of a uvcg_extension, whose item->ci_parent->ci_parent->ci_parent is the f_uvc_opts config_item; page is a PAGE_SIZE buffer. Postcondition: it takes the group's subsystem su_mutex, then opts->lock, writes sprintf(page, "%u\n", xu->desc.iExtension) (the extension unit descriptor field), releases both mutexes in reverse order and returns the number of bytes written (positive for an 8-bit value); there is no error return and the descriptor is not modified.
note: macro-generated; prose verified against lines 787-811

name: functionfs_acquire_dev
prose: functionfs_acquire_dev(dev) (g_ffs.c:256-262); dev is not used. Postcondition: if try_module_get(THIS_MODULE) fails it returns ERR_PTR(-ENOENT); otherwise it has taken a module reference and returns NULL. No lock is taken.
note: prose rechecked; static function with an ignored ffs_dev argument

name: functionfs_release_dev
prose: functionfs_release_dev(dev) (g_ffs.c:264-267); dev is not used. Postcondition: it calls module_put(THIS_MODULE) once and returns nothing; the caller is expected to hold a reference obtained with functionfs_acquire_dev.
note: prose rechecked

name: functionfs_ready_callback
prose: functionfs_ready_callback(ffs) (g_ffs.c:272-291); the source comment says the caller takes ffs_lock. Postcondition: it decrements missing_funcs; if the result is nonzero it returns 0. If it reached 0 and gfs_registered is already true it returns -EBUSY (missing_funcs stays decremented). Otherwise it sets gfs_registered = true and calls usb_composite_probe(&gfs_driver): on a negative result it increments missing_funcs again, sets gfs_registered = false and returns that result; otherwise it returns the probe result (0).
note: prose rechecked; added that missing_funcs is not restored on the -EBUSY path

name: functionfs_closed_callback
prose: functionfs_closed_callback(ffs) (g_ffs.c:296-303); the source comment says the caller takes ffs_lock. Postcondition: it increments missing_funcs; if gfs_registered is true it calls usb_composite_unregister(&gfs_driver); it then sets gfs_registered = false and returns nothing.
note: prose rechecked

name: gfs_bind
prose: gfs_bind(cdev) (g_ffs.c:308-435); the source comment says it is called with ffs_lock held. The set of function instances it takes depends on CONFIG_USB_FUNCTIONFS_ETH and CONFIG_USB_FUNCTIONFS_RNDIS. Postcondition: it returns -ENODEV at once if missing_funcs is nonzero. Otherwise, depending on the configuration, it gets the "ecm" or "geth" function instance and the "rndis" instance (a failing usb_get_function_instance returns its error; a failing "rndis" instance releases the ecm/geth instance first), configures the net device and, when both are configured, registers it with gether_register_netdev. It then calls usb_string_ids_tab, allocates the OTG descriptor if the gadget is OTG and none exists (-ENOMEM on failure), and adds each of the gfs_configurations with usb_add_config(cdev, &c->c, gfs_do_config). On success it calls usb_composite_overwrite_options and returns 0. On failure of usb_string_ids_tab, the OTG allocation or gether_register_netdev it releases the function instances it acquired; on a usb_add_config failure it also frees gfs_otg_desc[0] and sets it NULL first; configurations added before the failing one remain added. The failing call's negative errno is returned.
note: prose rechecked against the config-dependent paths; OTG descriptor is freed only on the usb_add_config failure path

name: gfs_unbind
prose: gfs_unbind(cdev) (g_ffs.c:440-465); the source comment says it is called with ffs_lock held. Postcondition: depending on the configuration it puts f_rndis and fi_rndis and puts f_ecm/fi_ecm or f_geth/fi_geth; it puts every f_ffs[0][i] for i from 0 up to N_CONF * func_num - 1, frees gfs_otg_desc[0], sets it to NULL and returns 0.
note: prose rechecked; the rndis/ecm/geth parts depend on CONFIG_USB_FUNCTIONFS_RNDIS/ETH

name: gfs_do_config
prose: gfs_do_config(c) (g_ffs.c:471-526); the source comment says ffs_lock is held. Postcondition: it returns -ENODEV at once if missing_funcs is nonzero. If the gadget is OTG it sets c->descriptors = gfs_otg_desc and adds USB_CONFIG_ATT_WAKEUP. If gc->eth is set it calls it and returns a negative result. Then for each of func_num ffs functions it gets f_ffs[gc->num][i] with usb_get_function (an error pointer is returned as its error) and adds it with usb_add_function (on failure that function is put first). On any failure it unwinds entries i-1 down to 0 (usb_remove_function unless the slot holds an error pointer, then usb_put_function) and returns the error. On success it sets c->interface[c->next_interface_id] to NULL if that index is inside the array and returns 0.
note: prose rechecked; ethernet config callback gc->eth added; the unwind loop starts at i-1

name: gadgetfs_setup
prose: Slice cut the head: gadgetfs_setup(gadget, ctrl) (inode.c:1336-1555). Precondition: get_gadget_data(gadget) is a live dev_data with dev->req, dev->dev, dev->config and dev->lock; ctrl is the ep0 setup packet. Postcondition: value starts as -EOPNOTSUPP. If wLength exceeds RBUF_SIZE, an OUT request returns -EOPNOTSUPP without taking dev->lock, and an IN request has ctrl->wLength overwritten with RBUF_SIZE (const cast) and continues. It takes dev->lock and clears setup_abort (or sets it to 1 if the state is STATE_DEV_SETUP). From STATE_DEV_UNCONNECTED it returns -EINVAL with the lock released if the gadget is dual-speed at high speed and dev->hs_config is NULL; otherwise it queues a GADGETFS_CONNECT event with the speed, sets STATE_DEV_CONNECTED and calls ep0_readable. It sets req->buf = dev->rbuf and req->context = NULL and dispatches on bRequest. GET_DESCRIPTOR (bRequestType must be USB_DIR_IN, else unrecognized): device descriptor from dev->dev (min(w_length, sizeof *dev->dev), bMaxPacketSize0 updated); qualifier built with make_qualifier only if dev->hs_config exists; config and other-speed config through config_buf (min(w_length, size), negative on error); USB_DT_STRING is unrecognized; other types leave value negative without delegation. SET_CONFIGURATION (bRequestType must be 0): a zero value sets current_config 0 and vbus draw 8 mA, a value equal to the configuration of the current speed sets current_config and vbus draw 2*bMaxPower, both give value 0, anything else leaves value negative; with value 0 the gadget state is set to configured and, if dev->usermode_setup is set, setup_can_stall = 0 and the request is delegated. GET_CONFIGURATION (bRequestType 0x80, not on PXA25X): writes current_config, value min(w_length, 1). The unrecognized cases (other request, mismatched request type, string descriptors) return -EOPNOTSUPP when dev->usermode_setup is NULL; otherwise setup_can_stall = 1 and the request is delegated. Delegation records setup_in, setup_wLength, setup_out_ready = 0 and setup_out_error = 0; for an OUT request with data it calls setup_req and then usb_ep_queue on ep0 (with the lock dropped for the queue), returns the negative result on failure (calling clean_req after a queue failure, not after a setup_req failure) and clears setup_can_stall on success; it then queues a GADGETFS_SETUP event with *ctrl, calls ep0_readable, releases the lock and returns USB_GADGET_DELAYED_STATUS if w_length is 0, else 0. For a non-delegated request with value >= 0 and dev->state != STATE_DEV_SETUP it sets req->length = value and zero = value < w_length, queues req on ep0 with the lock dropped, releases the lock and returns the usb_ep_queue result (clearing req->status on failure); with state STATE_DEV_SETUP it returns value without queueing. In all other cases it releases the lock and returns value. The lock is released on each return after it was taken.
note: reviewer WRONG (R15): with dev->state == STATE_DEV_SETUP the code does skip the queue (1535 'value >= 0 && dev->state != STATE_DEV_SETUP'), as the old prose said; R2's claim that standard requests are not queued is wrong (1535-1549); prose otherwise rechecked against all branches

name: raw_ioctl_init
prose: Slice cut the head: raw_ioctl_init(dev, value) (raw_gadget.c:480-577). Precondition: dev is a raw_dev; value is a user pointer to a struct usb_raw_init. Postcondition: it returns -EFAULT if the argument cannot be copied; the speed USB_SPEED_UNKNOWN is replaced by USB_SPEED_HIGH, LOW/FULL/HIGH/SUPER are kept and any other speed returns -EINVAL. It then allocates a driver id with ida_alloc (a negative result is returned), three kmalloc buffers (-ENOMEM on failure), formats the driver name DRIVER_NAME.<id> and copies the driver and device name strings with strscpy (a negative result such as -E2BIG is returned if one does not fit in UDC_NAME_LENGTH_MAX). Under dev->lock (irqsave) it returns -EINVAL if dev->state is not STATE_DEV_OPENED. Otherwise it stores udc_name, driver.function, max_speed = the chosen speed, the fixed callbacks setup, disconnect, bind, unbind, suspend, resume and reset, driver.driver.name, driver.udc_name, match_existing_only = 1 and driver_id_number, sets dev->state = STATE_DEV_INITIALIZED and returns 0. On every failure after the id allocation the buffers allocated so far and the id are freed and dev->state is left unchanged.
note: reviewer RIGHT (R15): the callbacks and match_existing_only are set by the function itself, not 'from arg' (548-559); only max_speed and the two names come from arg

name: ast_vhub_hub_wake_all
prose: Slice cut the head: ast_vhub_hub_wake_all(vhub) (aspeed-vhub/hub.c:589-599). Precondition: vhub->lock is held by the caller (lockdep_assert_held) and vhub is valid. Postcondition: it calls schedule_work(&vhub->wake_work) and returns nothing; the work is not run here and this function takes and releases no lock. schedule_work queues the work only if it is not already pending; if the work is currently running (and not pending) it is queued again, so the work function runs after this call in either case.
note: reviewer RIGHT (R15): schedule_work can queue a new instance while the work is running; old prose said nothing new is queued if it is 'pending or running'

name: at91_ep_queue
prose: Slice cut the head: at91_ep_queue(_ep, _req, gfp_flags) (at91_udc.c:605-703). Precondition: _ep and _req are the endpoint and request being queued. Postcondition: before taking any lock it returns -EINVAL if _req is NULL, has no complete callback or buffer, or is already on a queue, if _ep is NULL or has no descriptor and is not ep0, or if the endpoint's udc is NULL, has no driver or has an unknown gadget speed. It then sets _req->status = -EINPROGRESS and actual = 0 and takes udc->lock with interrupts saved. If the endpoint queue is empty and the endpoint is not stopped it tries to start the transfer: for ep0 it returns -EINVAL if udc->req_pending is clear, toggles CONFG when wait_for_config_ack is set, and for a zero-length ep0 request it sets TXPKTRDY and CLR_FX in the control register, clears req_pending and returns 0 without queueing; otherwise it calls write_fifo (IN) or read_fifo (OUT), and an ep0 OUT with a nonzero result takes the same IN/STATUS path. A negative result from write_fifo/read_fifo is returned. If the endpoint is stopped or its queue is non-empty the status is 0. When the status is exactly 0 the request is appended to ep->queue and ep->int_mask is written to AT91_UDP_IER; a positive result from write_fifo/read_fifo (the request was already completed) is not queued. The function returns the negative status or 0, and releases udc->lock on each return after it was taken.
note: reviewer RIGHT (R15): the three early -EINVAL returns happen before the lock is taken (617-633); old prose also said a 0 return always queues the request, but a positive write_fifo/read_fifo result (done) is not queued and returns 0 (696-702)

name: setup_received_irq
prose: Slice cut the head: setup_received_irq(udc, setup) (fsl_udc_core.c:1390-1513), called with udc->lock held (it drops and retakes it as annotated). Postcondition: returns nothing. It first calls udc_reset_ep_queue(udc, 0) (nuking ep0's queue with -ESHUTDOWN when ep0 has a name). Then by bRequest: GET_STATUS with a standard IN request calls ch9getstatus (which sets ep0_dir to IN, except that a request for an endpoint without a descriptor stalls before that; on success it queues the status data, sets ep0_state = DATA_STATE_XMIT and primes the OUT status, calling ep0stall if that fails, and its map/descriptor failures stall leaving ep0_state unchanged) and returns; SET_ADDRESS with an OUT standard device request calls ch9setaddress (stores the address, sets usb_state to USB_STATE_ADDRESS, primes the IN status and calls ep0stall if that fails) and returns; CLEAR/SET_FEATURE for a standard endpoint recipient with wValue 0, wLength 0 and a valid pipe calls fsl_ep_set_halt with the lock dropped, and for a standard device recipient handles TEST_MODE (portsc1 programmed after a 10 ms delay) or the OTG flags and treats the request as done; in those two cases, if the result is 0 it primes an IN status phase (ep0stall if that fails), and then returns; a nonzero fsl_ep_set_halt result returns without priming or stalling and without forwarding. Any request not handled above (including feature requests that fail the recipient or parameter checks) is forwarded to udc->driver->setup with the lock dropped (ep0stall if it returns negative): with wLength nonzero, ep0_dir is set to the request direction and ep0_state to DATA_STATE_XMIT (IN) or DATA_STATE_RECV (OUT), and for an IN request the OUT status is primed (ep0stall on failure); with wLength zero, ep0_dir is IN and ep0_state is WAIT_FOR_OUT_STATUS. udc->lock is held again on every return.
note: reviewer RIGHT (R15): ch9getstatus stalls for an unknown endpoint before setting ep0_dir (1351-1352, 1357); old prose also did not say that a failed fsl_ep_set_halt neither primes, stalls nor forwards

name: ehci_irq
prose: Slice cut the head: ehci_irq(hcd) (ehci-hcd.c:712-865). Precondition: the caller does not hold ehci->lock. Postcondition: it takes ehci->lock and reads the status register. If the status is all ones it goes straight to the dead path (before the IRQ_NONE checks, so even with rh_state HALTED). Otherwise the masked status is status & (INTR_MASK | STS_FLR); if that is zero or rh_state is EHCI_RH_HALTED it releases the lock and returns IRQ_NONE with nothing else done. Otherwise it writes the masked bits back to the status register, re-reads it and, while interrupt bits are set again, repeats, accumulating the bits into status. With STS_INT or STS_ERR set it increments stats.normal (no STS_ERR) or stats.error (forcing STS_PCD if has_ci_pec_bug) and sets bh. STS_IAA clears the IAA watchdog bit in enabled_hrtimer_events, advances next_hrtimer_event if it was the IAA watchdog, logs if CMD_IAAD is still set, counts stats.iaa when iaa_in_progress and calls end_iaa_cycle. STS_PCD records pcd_status, resumes the root hub if suspended and, for each port with a change bit (all ports when has_ppcd is false) that is not owned, is in suspended_ports, has PORT_PE set, is resuming or not suspended and has reset_done == 0, starts remote-wakeup resume signaling (reset_done, resuming_ports, usb_hcd_start_port_resume, mod_timer). STS_FATAL, like the all-ones case, takes the dead path: usb_hc_died, shutdown = true, rh_state = EHCI_RH_STOPPING, CMD_RUN/CMD_ASE/CMD_PSE cleared and written, intr_enable written 0, ehci_handle_controller_death, bh = 0. ehci_work is called only if bh is set. The lock is then released, usb_hcd_poll_rh_status is called if pcd_status is nonzero, and IRQ_HANDLED is returned from each return other than the IRQ_NONE one. In the all-ones case the status register is not written; in the STS_FATAL case the status bits were already cleared.
note: reviewer MIXED (R15): right that the all-ones check (726-729) precedes the HALTED/zero IRQ_NONE test, so the old wording was unclear; the prose otherwise matched the code, and R1/R2 points were conditional statements already

name: ehci_bus_suspend
prose: Slice cut the head: ehci_bus_suspend(hcd) (ehci-hub.c:213-372). Precondition: hcd is a valid EHCI root hub; the function itself takes ehci->lock (irq-disabling) and does not expect it held. Postcondition: it sleeps 5 ms if next_statechange has not passed, calls ehci_quiesce and takes the lock. If rh_state is below EHCI_RH_RUNNING it goes to the done tail (below) without touching ports or the controller. If the root hub has remote wakeup enabled and ehci->resuming_ports is nonzero it releases the lock and returns -EBUSY (the quiesce has already happened). Otherwise it clears bus_suspended and owned_ports, then for each port records PORT_OWNER ports in owned_ports, sets PORT_SUSPEND (and the bus_suspended bit) on enabled unsuspended ports, and with remote wakeup enabled sets the wake bits (WKOC plus WKDISC or WKCONN by connection state), writing the port register when it changed. After unlocking it applies the FSL suspend-errata and TDI-PHY-low-power/full-speed-idle delays, sets HOSTPC_PHCD on all ports when changed and has_tdi_phy_lpm, waits 150 us if any port was suspended and calls ehci_halt. Under the lock again it calls ehci_handle_controller_death if the POLL_DEAD event is pending; if rh_state is not then EHCI_RH_RUNNING it goes to done; otherwise rh_state = EHCI_RH_SUSPENDED, unlink_empty_async_suspended, STS_IAA is written to the status register, end_iaa_cycle, ehci_handle_start_intr_unlinks, ehci_handle_intr_unlinks and end_free_itds run, and intr_enable is written with INTR_MASK (STS_PCD removed when remote wakeup is disabled). The done tail sets next_statechange = jiffies + 10 ms, clears enabled_hrtimer_events, sets next_hrtimer_event = EHCI_HRTIMER_NO_EVENT, releases the lock, cancels ehci->hrtimer and returns 0. Each return other than the -EBUSY one returns 0.
note: reviewer MIXED (R15): the 'rh_state < EHCI_RH_RUNNING' early exit exists (230-231) and the old prose only hinted at it, but there is no ehci->shutdown test and ehci_quiesce has already run on that path; the function also does not depend on a root hub lock being held

name: ehci_platform_probe
prose: Slice cut the head: ehci_platform_probe(dev) (ehci-platform.c:237-401). Precondition: dev is the platform device; platform data may be absent (then ehci_platform_defaults is used and stored in dev->dev.platform_data). Postcondition: returns -ENODEV if USB is disabled; the DMA mask error; the platform_get_irq error if negative; -ENOMEM if usb_create_hcd fails (nothing acquired). After that platform drvdata is the HCD. With the defaults and an OF node it reads the OF flags and gets up to EHCI_MAX_CLKS clocks with of_clk_get (-EPROBE_DEFER is an error; other errors end the clock loop with a NULL entry). It then gets and deasserts the reset control array (failures go to the clock-release label), applies the platform data flags, returns -EINVAL if big-endian MMIO or descriptors were requested without the matching CONFIG option, calls pdata->power_on if set (a negative result is an error), maps register resource 0 and calls usb_add_hcd(hcd, irq, IRQF_SHARED). On success it enables device wakeup and async suspend, starts quirk polling if requested and returns 0. Failures of ioremap or usb_add_hcd call pdata->power_off whenever it is set (whether or not power_on exists), then assert the reset control; a failure of the endian checks or power_on asserts the reset control without power_off; a reset-control lookup or deassert failure releases only the clocks. All failure paths put the clocks that were obtained (the failing one is not put), clear dev->dev.platform_data if the defaults were used, call usb_put_hcd and return the error; the devm reset control and register mapping are released later by devres and the drvdata keeps pointing at the freed HCD.
note: reviewer RIGHT (R15): power_off is called on ioremap/usb_add_hcd failure if pdata->power_off is set, with no check that power_on ran (386-388); the reset-lookup failure also skips the assert (319-323)

name: iso_stream_schedule
prose: Slice cut the head: iso_stream_schedule(ehci, urb, stream) (ehci-sched.c:1471-1659). Precondition: urb->hcpriv is the ehci_iso_sched allocated for the URB and stream is the iso stream of its endpoint; mod is a local, ehci->periodic_size << 3. Postcondition: it returns 0 when a start slot was chosen, 1 when the whole URB lies in the past and the stream's td_list was empty, -EFBIG, -ENOSPC or the PTR_ERR of find_tt. When the stream is empty and no completion is in progress it picks a start: for a stream with no phase it finds a uframe slot with enough bandwidth (itd_slot_ok or sitd_slot_ok) and reserves the bandwidth, failing with the find_tt error or -ENOSPC ("iso sched full"); otherwise it uses the stream's existing phase; it sets stream->next_uframe to that start. It then compares with the current frame index. For an existing stream with non-empty queue and start < period it returns -EFBIG (the schedule would wrap). Depending on URB_ISO_ASAP and whether the start is in the past, it uses the start, a slot after the earliest allowed one, or skips packets: skip is rounded up to a multiple of the period; if skip reaches the span the skip is limited to span - period, or, if the stream was empty, set to span, the URB is reported as status 1, the iso_sched is freed with iso_sched_free and urb->hcpriv is set to NULL. In the skip path urb->error_count = skip / period and sched->first_packet (if sched is non-NULL) is set to that count; other paths do not change them. Finally if start + span - period >= mod + wrap it returns -EFBIG (this can follow a status 1 set above, with hcpriv already NULL); otherwise it sets stream->next_uframe = (start + skip) & (mod - 1) (the first scheduled slot plus the skip, not the slot after the last packet), urb->start_frame = start & (mod - 1) (shifted right by 3 for a non-high-speed stream) and returns status. It links no TDs and takes no lock itself.
note: reviewer RIGHT (R15): next_uframe = (start + skip) & (mod-1) (1649); old prose said it is the slot after the last packet, said error_count/first_packet are always set (only in the skip path), and treated mod as a precondition although it is a local

name: start_unlink_intr
prose: Slice cut the head: start_unlink_intr(ehci, qh) (ehci-sched.c:649-681). Precondition: ehci and qh are valid and the caller holds ehci->lock as for the other schedule functions; qh is an interrupt QH. Postcondition: it returns at once with no effect if qh->qh_state is not QH_STATE_LINKED. Otherwise cancel_unlink_wait_intr removes qh from a wait list with list_del_init if its unlink_node is non-empty, qh_unlink_periodic removes qh from every periodic schedule slot of its period, lowers the controller's bandwidth_allocated, sets qh->qh_state = QH_STATE_UNLINK, clears qh->qh_next.ptr, advances ehci->qh_scan_next if it pointed at qh and removes qh from the intr_node list. Then a write barrier is issued, qh->unlink_cycle is set to ehci->intr_unlink_cycle and qh is appended to the tail of ehci->intr_unlink. After that: if ehci->intr_unlinking is set nothing more is done; else if rh_state is below EHCI_RH_RUNNING, ehci_handle_intr_unlinks is called at once; else if qh is the first entry of intr_unlink the EHCI_HRTIMER_UNLINK_INTR event is enabled and ehci->intr_unlink_cycle is incremented; otherwise nothing more. It returns nothing.
note: reviewer RIGHT (R15): the write barrier is before the unlink_cycle assignment and list_add_tail (661-671), not after; the old prose said 'after a write barrier' for the intr_unlinking test

name: postproc_atl_queue
prose: Slice cut the head: postproc_atl_queue(isp116x) (isp116x-hcd.c:348-474). Precondition: the caller holds isp116x->lock; atl_active is NULL or a chain linked through ->active in which each endpoint has a non-empty urb_list (BUG_ON otherwise). Postcondition: for each endpoint in the chain it looks at the first urb and the ptd completion code cc. A data underrun with an allowed underrun or a control pipe is treated as no error (short_not_ok = 0); a forbidden underrun sets ep->error_count = 1, the toggle bit, adds the ptd count to urb->actual_length and ends the urb with the underrun error status. Another completion code other than no-error/not-accessed increments ep->error_count and, at 3 errors or on STALL or DATAOVERRUN, ends the urb with the mapped error status (nextpid ACK becomes 0), without updating actual_length. An interrupt transfer with zero ptd length ends with status 0. Otherwise error_count is cleared on success, the toggle is set from the ptd according to nextpid, and for IN/OUT stages actual_length += the ptd count and the urb ends (status 0, or nextpid becomes ACK for control) when the ptd is complete and the length rules are met; SETUP moves to the data, IN/OUT or ACK stage; ACK ends the urb with status 0 and nextpid 0. If the status is not -EINPROGRESS or the urb is unlinked, finish_request(isp116x, ep, urb, status) is called, so an unlinked urb can be given back with -EINPROGRESS; finish_request resets error_count, moves a control endpoint back to the SETUP pid, unlinks the urb, drops and retakes isp116x->lock around usb_hcd_giveback_urb and deschedules an idle endpoint. Other urbs stay queued. The lock is held again on return.
note: reviewer RIGHT (R15): an unlinked urb is passed to finish_request with the status still -EINPROGRESS (471-472); also the error_count>=3/STALL path skips actual_length and toggle updates and the toggle/length updates happen for forbidden underrun and IN/OUT stages
